New data reveals that UK public bodies spent £3.4 billion on private consultants last year, marking a 62% increase since 2019-20. This surge in spending has persisted beyond the pandemic, posing a challenge to the new Labour government, which has pledged to reduce these costs by half. Recent deals include a significant training contract for KPMG worth up to £223 million. Critics such as Prem Sikka have labeled the situation scandalous, arguing that the heavy reliance on outside firms offers little value to the public sector.
